page: Microsoft Azure E16bds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 614 GB of SSD capacity.

Benchmark results place this server in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1899.09 and a multi-core score of 15534.8, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector extensions. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 839.97 GB/sec, dropping to 102.72 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In database operations, the instance handles 15.88 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 7921.71 on PassMark database tests.

Lacking dedicated GPU hardware, the server is not suited for large-scale deep learning training, as shown by the lack of 70B LLM inference data and modest 7B model generation speeds of 11.61 tokens/sec. However, its high memory density, local SSD storage, and solid block storage capabilities make it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of GPU resources. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
